- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias in next 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward correction for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum, not just price history.
